html:
The Battle of Paardeberg was fought from 18 to 27 February 1900 on the Modder River in the Orange Free State, now in South Africa. A British army trapped the Boer general Piet Cronjé, who surrendered with about 4,000 men.

It was the first big British victory of the Second Boer War, after months of defeats. The Boers of the Orange Free State and the Transvaal had besieged Kimberley, Ladysmith and Mafeking. In February 1900 Lord Roberts arrived with a much larger army, and his cavalry relieved Kimberley. Cronjé retreated east with his wagons and families and was caught at a river crossing. On 18 February, later called Bloody Sunday, Lord Kitchener ordered direct attacks on the Boer camp. They failed, with over 1,000 men killed or wounded. Roberts then surrounded the camp and shelled it for a week.

Cronjé gave up on 27 February, the anniversary of the Boer victory at Majuba in 1881. Roberts took Bloemfontein in March and Pretoria in June. But the Boers turned to guerrilla war, and the British Empire answered with farm burning and concentration camps. The war lasted until 1902.
